title: Fieller-Type Confidence Sets for Budget-Constrained Invalid-Instrument Identified Sets
banked_reason: D-0.5 angle 0 exhausted five revisions after reviewer REVISE; v5 remained field with S=0 N=0 C=1 but found a new rotating published-BudgetIV budget-domain coherence defect after the whole-core audit.
gap_reasons: The model is called an independent two-sample experiment while allowing arbitrary within-pair covariance B_j; genuinely independent exposure and outcome GWAS summaries have B_j=0, so either impose B_j=0 or rename and define a correlated/overlapping-summary Gaussian experiment.

The core calls Gamma the published BudgetIV class but permits b1=0 and weakly increasing budgets, whereas Penn et al.'s published BudgetIV definition requires 0<b1<⋯<bK; impose those inequalities or explicitly rename this as a generalized redundant-tier extension.
proof_attempt_summary: Angle 0 developed a field-rated exact-Gaussian quota-envelope and certified inversion proposal, resolving successive sanity, domain, q-versus-q-plus, exact-arithmetic, and paired-summary model-scope defects. The fifth review found a new published-BudgetIV budget-domain mismatch after a whole-core audit, so the anti-rotation cap terminated the run before Stage D0 or any Lean proof attempt. The mathematical kernel was not refuted; a future retry should begin with 0 < b1 < ⋯ < bK and preserve the paired-summary terminology.
tldr: The field-level kernel is a new completeness theorem for a graded-quota lower envelope: balanced min-cost flow, every simple exchange cycle, and equality-complete polynomial sign decomposition together enumerate every BudgetIV interval, singleton, and ray without a bounded grid. In the fixed-\(p\), fixed-finite-\(K\), block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment with known covariance, projection of one joint ellipsoid also gives finite-sample uniform containment of the entire population identified set, while a cutoff-indexed trimmed first-stage statistic and lexicographic certificate resolve both tails separately at \(q\) and \(q^+\). Arbitrary known \(B_j\) permits correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries within each instrument; genuinely independent disjoint two-sample GWAS is exactly the submodel \(B_j=0\). This exact coverage is not a guarantee for estimated covariance or residual linkage disequilibrium; exact-\(q\) termination is oracle-relative for arbitrary-real inputs, while unconditional conservative arithmetic at \(q^+\) requires every threshold, budget, observed summary, covariance entry, and \(q^+\) used in boundary coefficients to be rational or real algebraic and rebuilds the finite-root and tail certificates at that cutoff; endpoint and label recovery is confined to the primitive positive-width regular-face domain with stable pairing, unique active labels, and a positive exchange-cycle margin, excluding zero first stages, tangencies, shrinking gaps, exchange ties, singletons, and other nonregular components.
gap: Penn et al. leave inference without NOME open; pointwise weak-IV and invalid-IV procedures do not supply simultaneous containment of a disconnected BudgetIV population set; and root-based ordinary-IV inversion does not handle a lower envelope over nested quota assignments.
fill: The project derives the projection cost and whole-set coverage inside the block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment, allowing known within-pair covariance from correlated or overlapping summaries and specializing to disjoint two-sample summaries at \(B_j=0\). It then makes the quota-flow exchange-cycle completeness and equality-complete certified topology inversion the field-level result. The first open validation deliverable is an explicit rational \(p=3\), \(K=2\) certificate exhibiting an optimizer-changing cycle, an equality-tail decision, and exhaustive-assignment agreement, followed by a one-hundred-instance comparison.
